_comment: Per-movie context the render_model export cannot carry, because it lived in
Lingo movie scripts rather than in the score. Hand maintained.
NOT under assets/ on purpose: assets/SOURCE.txt documents that tree as
mirrored with `robocopy /MIR`, which would delete this file.
_transitions_comment: Destination room for a walk transition that ends on the dynamic redirect
handler (frame_script 207). Without an entry the score falls into the
adjacent reverse animation and Piposh walks back where he came from.
Destinations are NOT derivable from the export: walk navs carry only
target_label / walk_to / arrive_at, the hosting room is always the source,
and name rules contradict each other (swingup -> swing, but path3up ->
path4 and shore2up -> gate). Entries are added only once verified.
'shared' applies to every movie. DAY1 and NIGHT1 are the same island by
day and by night, so the verified Day 1 destinations also resolve 19 of
NIGHT1's 27 transitions. A per-movie block overrides 'shared'.
_progression_comment: THE PROGRESSION SPINE. Everything here is INFERRED, not sourced.
The original rules live in Lingo (peoplefunk and the day handlers) which
is not available. Without these rules the game cannot advance past day 1
at all, so they exist as scaffolding: the game becomes completable, and
every line is one edit away from correct once the Lingo is recovered.
Each entry carries a confidence note. Treat none of it as faithful.

meeting_triggers.confidence: good — recept carries a mantalk label and ISHDAY1 returns to receptfromish; ish is the man at reception
moderate — the movie name reads TOFI-ReCePT and it returns to retlobi; ordered after ISHDAY1 so both do not fire in one room
weak — only signal is that ALLIN returns to prosdor, and a return label does not prove the trigger room (HATDAY1 triggers at veranda and returns to gate)
good — NIGHT1 shore3go carries cast 1:217, the same corpse sprite as DAY1 shore3, so the body is found on the night beach

_phase_transitions_comment: When a hub hands over to the next one. Fires on arrival in a room once no
meeting is due. require_meetings names meetings-list entries that must all

phase_transitions.confidence: inferred — day 1 ends once its seven meetings are done; the real condition is unknown and there is no DAY1 to NIGHT1 edge anywhere in the score

_day_advance_comment: Arriving at one of these movie/label pairs sets globalday. SLEEP1 and
SLEEP2 both route to HOTEL1 newmorning in the exported score, so the
morning label is the natural place for the day to turn over.

day_advance.label: newmorning
day_advance.confidence: good — SLEEP1 and SLEEP2 both declare hotel1 @newmorning as their return in the exported data

_click_flags_comment: Hotspots that exist to reveal something else: clicking the sand turns up
the shells. Clicking a listed channel raises 'sets_flag', and a sprite
gate can then wait on it with 'after_flag'. Flags persist in saves.
Empty until the reveal hotspots are identified in play.
_sprite_gates_comment: Director rooms carry every conditional character and object at once, and
Lingo puppeted away whatever the story had not reached. The export keeps
the sprites but not the conditions, so the runtime draws everything: NPCs
stand in rooms on days they should not, and event aftermath is visible
before the event. Declare the conditions here; they gate both drawing and
clicking. A room name covers its 'go' variant too (shore3 = shore3go).
Conditions form a window, because content can be premature (a corpse
before the murder) or stale (a character still sitting where they were
before a conversation moved them). Every condition has both forms:
after_meeting / before_meeting  a meetings-list entry, e.g. murder1
after_flag / before_flag        a flag raised by click_flags above
All listed conditions must hold. Absent means always visible.
This table is far from complete. Add a rule whenever play shows content

_unmapped_comment: Known-missing destinations: 46 movie/label pairs, 40 distinct labels.
Recovering them needs the original Lingo (nextroomdata) or playtesting.
Each logs an 'unmapped transition' warning naming movie and label. Move a
label into 'transitions' as soon as its destination is confirmed.
